chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Safwan, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, from Abi Basir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

«The Mutamatti' (one performing Hajj al-Tamattu'), if he performs Tawaf and Sa'i, then says Talbiyah before shaving/cutting his hair, he is not allowed to shave/cut his hair, and he does not have the reward of Tamattu'.» This is applicable to one who did it intentionally. As for one who did it forgetfully, his Umrah is not invalidated, according to what we have previously stated. This confirms what we have stated that his Umrah is not invalidated if he did it forgetfully, as narrated:

key_terms.الْمُتَمَتِّعُ: One performing Hajj al-Tamattu' (Umrah then Hajj)
key_terms.سَعَى: Performed Sa'i (walking between Safa and Marwah)
key_terms.يُقَصِّرَ: Shaves or cuts hair (sign of exiting Ihram)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a Mutamatti' pilgrim says Talbiyah before shaving his hair?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the conditions of Hajj al-Tamattu', distinguishing between intentional and forgetful errors in the sequence of Talbiyah and Qasr. This distinction underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that minor ritual deviations do not invalidate the Umrah unless performed deliberately, ensuring the pilgrim retains the spiritual merit of the Tamattu' type.
